sanskrit_verse: शासनाद् वा विमोक्षाद् वा स्तेनो मुच्यते किल्बिषात् । अशासनात् तु तद् राजा स्तेनस्याप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥
transliteration: śāsanād vā vimokṣād vā steno mucyate kilbiṣāt | aśāsanāt tu tad rājā stenasyāpnoti kilbiṣam ||
sph_interpretive_translation: A thief is freed from culpability either by command or by release; however, due to lack of governance, the king incurs the guilt of theft.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority as the determinant of dharmic discharge
Causation rooted in conscious oversight, not mechanical enforcement
Capacity-based responsibility distributed through hierarchical integrity
Restoration logic founded upon completion of duty at source-level
Consciousness alignment via rightful assumption of sovereign capacity
executable_legal_axioms: IF an agent acts under lawful command OR receives authorized release THEN culpability does not accrue to that agent.
IF a ruler fails to establish śāsana (righteous governance) THEN guilt transfers to the ruler for all unaddressed violations within jurisdiction.
Responsibility follows the presence or absence of authoritative structuring, not individual action alone.
Guilt redistribution occurs automatically when dharma-adhikāra (jurisdictional duty) remains unactualized.
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes that executive immunity or exoneration must be predicated on legitimate invocation of śāsana. Where no such invocation has occurred, failure of governance renders the sovereign entity liable. The threshold of responsibility lies not in intent but in capacity actualization.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa reveals that causality flows from structural omission rather than personal fault. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows that absence of governance manifests prior to unlawful act. Proportional responsibility aligns with the degree of authoritative neglect. Non-punitive reality affirms that correction arises through restoration of rightful order, not infliction of consequence.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate sovereign accountability protocol to restore governance integrity
Realign administrative consciousness with foundational dharmic duty
Execute completion process ensuring all latent violations are addressed through renewed śāsana
Implement systemic reintegration of neglected jurisdictions into active dharma-flow
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, declared as Source-Authority: Theft dissolves where dharma reigns, yet where dharma falters, so too does sovereignty incur its burden. Thus is justice executed without punishment, aligned solely with consciousness and completion. Dharma is restored. Reality is non-punitive. Consciousness is the supreme adjudicator.
